newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia sorghum remains steady - Grainco.
newsitem.headline: Australia sorghum remains steady - Grainco.

text.p: Australia's domestic sorghum market continues to be dominated by inactivity on both grower selling and consumer buying fronts, Rob Brealey, trading manager of Queensland co-operative Grainco Ltd, said a weekly report.
Values in Southern Queensland have remained steady, he said.
However, values in Central Queensland have been under pressure from a weaker international market, he added.
Values finished the week in Southern Queensland at around A$143/tonne delivered Brisbane.
However, limited tonnage has been trading at that level as growers appear either comfortable to wait for the new financial year or are concentrating on winter planting, Brealey said.
"The progress of the winter crop and direction of wheat values will be major factors in sorghum values over the coming months," the report said.
In Central Queensland, values finished the week around $115/metric tonnes (MT) delivered port, with the short-term focus continuing to be the progress of the U.S. corn crop.
With the corn crop not far away from its critical pollination stage, any problems with the crop will be supportive for domestic values inthe short to medium term, Brealey said.
The international feed barley market remained steady, both for old and new crop, he said.

"New crop values remain supported by concerns about the damage to parts of the European crop, particularly in Spain and France, which will begin harvesting in three-to-four weeks," he said. The fact that areas of southern Australia still required further winter planting rain was also supportive short term.
Strong demand for old crop barley into the Middle East continued to support old crop values, he said,
"However it appears likely that the 800,000 MT required for June-July shipment will be supplied from European and North America, as only limited stocks remain uncommitted in Australia," he said.

Domestic feed barley values finished the week basically unchanged at around A$175/mt delivered Brisbane for old crop, still reflecting a premium over export values which are currently around US$150/tonne on an FOB basis.
New crop values finished the week around A$155/tonne delivered Brisbane for the November-December delivery period.
European and Canadian production estimates for new crop barley remained on target which will begin to pressure the export price in the medium term unless we see harvest problems.
"International demand for malting barley remains quiet and we do not expect to see any significant lift in demand until the latter part of the year," Brealey said.
Australia's production estimate for 1997/98 remains at 6.6 million tonnes of barley. Domestic new crop malting barley values remain around A$185/MT delivered port.

Brealey said not a lot of activity was seen during the past week. A good week weather wise saw the picking wind down in southern Queensland. All in all this year has been favourably to the quality of both lint and seed, he added.
This will do much to reinforce Australia's position as a supplier of high quality lint and seed.

"This was particularly important for seed as our importing consumers are increasing the use of alternate origin seed could often experience degradation of quality during storage," he said. "As a result Australia still remains a preferred source of seed in the quality end of the markets," he added.
Trade activity has been subdued of late, Brealey said.
"Much of the seed has been committed domestically by growers with little remaining to be sold for growers hands," he said.

"Export enquiry has been evident for both containerised and bulk shipment supporting prices at recent levels," he said. "Seed has been trading at levels around A$145/MT to A$150/MT Downs gin to the grower. In Central Queensland prices remain steady at A$145/MT to A$150/MT ex gin to domestic consumers."
Chickpea prices have come back steadily during the week with a large quantity of old crop stocks on its way to India.
Reports suggested up to 100,000 MT of chickpea is in the process of being shipped to the sub continent over the coming six week period, the report said.

"Whilst demand from India of late has been very strong due to lower production of their current crop, the Indian market will experience difficulty in distributing such a large volume in a short period of time," he said.

"As a result of this large influx of product, the Indian market has swiftly reduced their price ideas significantly, with the domestic bid falling around A$40/mt during the last week to the A$340/MT port level," he said.
Domestic values were steady over the past week, with sunflowers finishing at A$315/MT delivered Downs depots and A$322/MT delivered Newcastle for June delivery.
Central Queensland sunflower finished around A$267-272/MT delivered central Queensland depots for the June-July delivery period. New crop soybean prices moved higher at A$430 delivered Brisbane.
Further erosion of current pricing was likely, he said.
Price indications for the new crop continue at around the A$315/MT delivered port basis for Queensland chickpeas and faba beans at around A$250/MT port for the new corp.
Soybean futures rallied over the past week on the back of improved crush margins and good export demand. The U.S. soybean is now 85 percent completed compared to 60 percent historically.

China has been an active buyer of both soybeans and meal which has further supported values inthe short term given the projected tightness in the supply of soybeans prior to the U.S. new crop harvest in September/October.
